description: Centenarians/nonagenarians vs younger controls genotyped at hypothesis-driven SNPs (IIS, lipids, inflammation, antioxidants).
strengths: Cheap; biologically motivated; built most of HAGR LongevityMap.
blind_spots: Small n; younger controls born decades later (cohort/birth-period confounding); ancestry mismatch; winner's curse; publication bias. Model-organism plausibility (e.g., SIRT1) often fails in humans; few loci beyond APOE/FOXO3 replicate.
implication_for_module: Most v1 rows. Downgrade single-study candidate rows by default; mark design in studies.csv; never present as established.

description: Pooling published case-control studies per variant to obtain pooled ORs.
strengths: Gives pooled OR+CI; exposes heterogeneity and null results (PON1, IL6 overall).
blind_spots: Inherits biased inputs; phenotype and control definitions differ; can inflate false negatives or bias estimates; sex/ancestry subgroup findings (FOXO3 males, IL6 Italian males, CETP direction flip) are fragile.
implication_for_module: Use pooled ORs for the few meta-analysed variants (APOE, ACE, FOXO3, CETP, KL, IL6) in effect_size/effect_measure. Encode nulls as non-protective states with a 'replication_failed' or 'meta_null' flag.

description: Cases defined as surviving beyond the 90th/99th (or top 1%) birth-cohort survival percentile; controls ≤60th percentile.
strengths: Birth-cohort-standardised phenotype; separates extreme-survival variants from mortality-selection artefacts.
blind_spots: Very limited power (thousands of cases); few genome-wide hits (APOE, GPR78 region, CDKN2B-AS1); ancestry-restricted.
implication_for_module: Record the percentile threshold per claim (studies.csv). APOE ε2/ε4 are the robust anchors. Report 'odds of reaching ≥90th/99th percentile', not 'lifespan years'.

description: GWAS of genotyped participants against their parents' age at death/attained age (UK Biobank, LifeGen).
strengths: Huge n (≈1M parental lifespans); many replicated loci; enables MR and PGS.
blind_spots: Proxy dilutes effect by ~half (one parent shares 50% of alleles); dominated by disease and behaviour loci (APOE, LPA, CHRNA3/5 smoking, CDKN2B-AS1); European-centric; tells about mid-late-life mortality more than extreme longevity.
implication_for_module: Label phenotype 'parental lifespan' distinctly. Expect such loci to be disease-mediated; cross-link to disease modules instead of double counting.

description: Healthspan (age at first chronic disease), or genetic factors combining healthspan, lifespan, longevity, frailty, self-rated health (mvAge, aging-GIP1).
strengths: Boosts power; captures shared ageing biology; discovers new loci (SLC4A7, haem metabolism; LPA/VCAM1).
blind_spots: Composite traits are hard to interpret per-allele; heavy UK Biobank/European overlap; effect sizes not on a lifespan scale.
implication_for_module: Allow phenotype values healthspan/multivariate_ageing. Treat as separate evidence lines from 'extreme longevity'.

approach: familial longevity scoring and family designs
description: LRC, FLoSS and ancestral-longevity counts to select heritable longevity cases; sib-pair linkage; offspring-of-centenarian designs.
strengths: Removes phenocopies; shows longevity is transmitted from top-10% survivors and ≥20% long-lived relatives; offspring show compression of morbidity.
blind_spots: Family-specific rare variants rarely replicate; familial advantage fades by ~100 years; data mainly European/US.
implication_for_module: README should state that a family history of longevity carries information that genotype rows do not capture. Optional user input (family history) is out of scope for genotype-only scoring.

description: Twin, pedigree and population-tree estimates, corrected for assortative mating or extrinsic mortality.
strengths: Bounds what genetics can explain.
blind_spots: Estimates span <10% (assortative-mating corrected pedigrees) to >50% (intrinsic mortality, 2026); they depend on cohort era and how extrinsic death is handled; not individual-level.
implication_for_module: README: present the range and the 2026 debate. Never imply an individual's lifespan is X% genetic.

description: Compare GWAS disease risk allele counts or PRS (AD, CAD, T2D, cancer) between long-lived and controls.
strengths: Tests whether longevity = absence of risk. Shows mixed answer: overall burden similar, but AD and CAD risk depleted in the healthiest/longest-lived.
blind_spots: Depends on which PRS; trade-offs (higher SCZ/T2D PRS in Chinese centenarians); small centenarian samples.
implication_for_module: Link variant rows to disease PGS rather than re-encoding disease alleles as 'longevity' alleles. Report: 'long-lived people carry many risk alleles too'.

description: Exome/genome sequencing of centenarians, supercentenarians and biobanks; gene burden tests.
strengths: Identifies protective rare alleles (SIRT6, IIS/AMPK, mTOR genes) and lifespan-shortening LoF (BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2).
blind_spots: Rare variants are mostly family- or population-private; burden signals are gene-level not variant-level; CH contaminates blood-derived calls (TET2, ASXL1, DNMT3A).
implication_for_module: Gene-level burden cannot be a variants.csv row. Use README/gene notes. Flag CH genes as possibly somatic. Defer BRCA1/2/ATM to ACMG modules.

description: Genotype frequency trajectories across ages; buffered-deleterious genotypes; antagonistic pleiotropy and age-sign-flipping effects.
strengths: Explains why risk alleles persist in centenarians and why effects invert with age.
blind_spots: Hard to estimate; few human datasets with dense age bins; mouse evidence dominates age-inversion.
implication_for_module: Add flag 'age_dependent_effect' / 'conditional_on_genotype' (e.g., MTP buffered by other genotypes; Wnt variants in APOE4 carriers).

description: Weighted sums of lifespan/longevity GWAS variants (PLS, iLGS, longevity PRS).
strengths: Shows ~4-5 year differences between extreme deciles; partly offsets APOE ε4.
blind_spots: Small per-person predictive value (HR ~0.7–1.2; time-dependent); European training data; sensitive to population structure.
implication_for_module: Point to PGS Catalog entries via the pgs table, not to an ad-hoc sum of variants.csv weights. Report deciles with uncertainty.

approach: Mendelian randomization (risk factor, drug target, omics)
description: Genetic instruments for exposures, proteins, CpGs, gene expression tested against lifespan/longevity.
strengths: Prioritises causal modifiable factors (LDL/PCSK9, BMI, BP, IL6R, LPA, VCAM1) and causal CpGs.
blind_spots: Pleiotropy; survival bias; European instruments; tells population average causal effects, not individual predictions.
implication_for_module: Add a flag such as 'mr_supported' for rows where the locus' mediator has MR support. Show it as the actionable layer in the report (modifiable exposures).

approach: omics ageing clocks (proteomic, metabolomic, epigenetic, organ-specific)
description: Machine-learned biological-age predictors from plasma proteins, metabolites, methylation; organ-specific clocks.
strengths: Measurable, modifiable, and strongly predictive of mortality; may capture resilience to APOE4.
blind_spots: Not genotype-derived; platform-specific; validation incomplete; correlation not causation (except causal clocks).
implication_for_module: Out of scope for genotype rows. README pointer: genotype is weaker than measured biomarkers; avoid implying genetic 'biological age'.

description: Exposome-wide association plus PRS to partition mortality variance; PRS × lifestyle joint effects.
strengths: Quantifies the small share of mortality explained by common genetics (<2 pp) vs exposome (17 pp).
blind_spots: Observational exposome; UKB volunteer bias; European.
implication_for_module: Report must contextualise: lifestyle effects (HR ~1.8) exceed genetic predisposition (HR ~1.2) and are additive.

description: Grouping loci into conserved pathways or hallmarks; interactome modules; co-expression enrichment of GWAS signals.
strengths: Interpretable grouping; links weak single-SNP signals to biology; consistent five pathways (IIS, DDR, immunity, cholesterol, telomeres).
blind_spots: Hallmarks are not causal paradigms; gene-set enrichment is not per-variant evidence; risk of circularity with model-organism priors.
implication_for_module: Replace v1 'other' (483/1022 rows) with a controlled pathway vocabulary in category. Display grouping only; no pathway-sum score.

description: Long-lived species genomes (bowhead, naked mole-rat, rockfish, beaver), convergent evolution, cross-species transcriptomes; functional tests in human cells.
strengths: Nominates mechanisms (DNA repair, CIRBP, cGAS, aryl-hydrocarbon metabolism) and gene sets enriched in human lifespan heritability.
blind_spots: Species-specific substitutions are almost never polymorphic in humans (81.2% invariant; 99.78% <1%); cannot become genotype rows.
implication_for_module: Gene-level 'comparative support' annotation (README or a gene-level side table). No variants.csv rows from species data.

description: Clonal haematopoiesis, mosaic chromosomal alterations, somatic mutation rates across species and tissues.
strengths: Explains TET2/ASXL1/DNMT3A lifespan signals; centenarians carry fewer mCAs.
blind_spots: Somatic burden is not germline; generally weak evidence as a driver of ageing (except cancer); needs VAF-aware calling.
implication_for_module: Flag CH-gene variants with low VAF as 'possible_somatic'; module output should say germline-only interpretation is assumed.

approach: long-read structural variant and repeat analysis
description: Nanopore/PacBio genomes resolving SVs, VNTRs, telomere length.
strengths: Recovers >60% of SVs missed by short reads; VNTRs (TERT) linked to centenarian status.
blind_spots: Early, small, preprint-level for ageing; not yet longevity-GWAS scale.
implication_for_module: Use requires_callable/callable_from for indel/repeat variants (e.g., ACE I/D); mark 'not assessable from short-read/array' in report.

description: Variant-effect predictors (AlphaMissense), LLM biological age, AI target discovery, AI-assisted meta-analysis.
strengths: Scales annotation; prioritises rare missense variants; new biological-age proxies.
blind_spots: Pathogenicity is not longevity effect; most ageing-AI lacks validation (3% in vivo).
implication_for_module: Optional computed annotation column for missense rare variants (score source + version). Never use as association evidence.

approach: N-of-1 deep phenotyping of extreme agers
description: Multi-omics of individual supercentenarians and the world's oldest person.
strengths: Hypothesis-generating; shows CH, telomere attrition coexist with health.
blind_spots: n=1; not generalisable.
implication_for_module: No rows. Cite only in README as context.
